present_on_scene_date.note: Documented teaching in 1833-34 and nothing reached follows him to 1835. By the winter of 1834-35 Andreas has George Davis opening a school on Lake Street over a store between Dearborn and Clark, and later in 1835 teaching in the Presbyterian church, which is a different man in a different room.

persons.name: Grenville Temple Sproat

occupation.note: 'The lower story was a hall for religious services, the upper floor was a school-room, where Granville Temple Sproat kept one of the first public schools.' The Chicago Democrat of 26 November 1833 independently reports a school established in the village by Mr Sproat of Boston, already running on the day the paper appeared.

persons.note: DOCUMENTED CONTEMPORANEOUSLY AND RETROSPECTIVELY, WITH AN ORIGIN IN THE CONTEMPORARY SOURCE - which makes this the only origin in the parcel that comes from a Chicago document rather than from a memoir. Andreas spells the forename both Granville and Grenville and the index carries 'Sproot, Grenville Temple'; his English and Classical School for Boys occupied the upper storey of the Temple Building. Two women are named as teachers in the same building at different times - 'Miss Chappel (Mrs. Jeremiah Porter), Miss Sarah Warren (Mrs. Abel E. Carpenter), and S. L. Carpenter' - and none of the three is written as a household here because none of them is placed in the town on any date near the scene date.

resident_research.evidence_for: Early education histories identify Granville T. Sproat opening an English and Classical School in Chicago in fall 1833 and Sarah L. Warren assisting him in March 1834. The source's Granville spelling is retained as a variant against the repository's Grenville spelling rather than silently normalized.

refusals.refusal_says: the ladder ABSTAINS (rule G5): every appearance this consolidation can see describes a date after the scene year, and the card rests on sources outside the seven domains it reads. G5 exists to decline to demote such a person on later evidence, and a pass that read the abstention as a verdict would be doing the one thing the rule forbids.

research_note: THE SCHOOLMASTER OF THE TOWN'S FIRST PURPOSE-BUILT SCHOOLROOM, and a household whose presence at the scene date is genuinely open. THE PARCEL'S SCHOOLING GAP IS WORTH STATING: in a town of 3,265 people this dataset can name three teachers - Watkins, Sproat and Eliza Chappel - of whom one is documented at work in the scene year, one is uncertain and one had married and left. George Davis, teaching on Lake Street in the winter of 1834-35 and in the Presbyterian church later in 1835, is a fourth and is the most obviously missing household in this parcel.
